text.insert: Each game has one harness worktree and durable timeline. Epochs, Sync operations, save points, and control events record progress within the harness.

Timeline entries carry game and harness identity, event and command IDs, numeric durable order, occurrence time, outcome, optional run/epoch/Sync IDs, source transitions, evidence, and recovery context. Active kinds include initial_sync_accepted, sandbox_validated, epoch_completed, sync_completed, remote_application, epoch_admitted, pause_requested, resumed, failed, and save_point. Reads filter by game with after/before cursors and ascending or descending order.

fields.name: identity
fields.description: Game/harness ID, stable event ID, durable order, timestamp, and causal command.

fields.name: kind
fields.description: Boundary kind, including initial Sync, epoch, Sync, sandbox validation, control, and evidence events.

fields.name: source
fields.description: Prior/resulting heads, prior/accepted upstream revisions, and configuration identity.

fields.name: evidence
fields.description: Save-point ID, report/artifact references, metric scope, freshness, and source manifests.

fields.name: recovery
fields.description: Failure stage and durable resume position. A retry keeps boundary identity.

rows: Initial Sync accepted
Initialized worktree identity, upstream revision, configuration provenance, and initial save point.
Establishes the first accepted harness head.
Epoch settled
Epoch identity, input head, accepted output head, outcomes, and epoch save point.
Advances the head only when integration accepted source changes.
Sync settled
Sync identity, prior and resulting heads, prior and accepted upstream revisions, source refresh outcomes, and evidence references.
Advances the head only when source reconciliation changes it. A no-change Sync still records completion.
Next epoch admitted
Epoch identity, accepted head, report provenance, and selected knowledge/index versions or watermarks.
Starts work from the accepted post-sync state without moving head.
Pause, failure, or resume
Requested action, settled work, blockers, causal operation, and recovery result.
Does not manufacture a source revision or end the harness.

text.insert: Epoch evidence measures worker progress before the following Sync. Post-sync evidence measures the reconciled checkout. Attribute these deltas separately so upstream improvements are not reported as worker gains. Compare matching scores only when their target scope, build configuration, and metric definition agree.

The next epoch refreshes report truth and board eligibility against the accepted post-sync head. Historical measurements remain attached to their original revisions; refreshing the baseline does not reset history. Source-stable Sync can reuse verified build evidence when its build inputs are unchanged, while recording separate knowledge refresh outcomes.

Persist a recoverable boundary for accepted head changes and their timeline entries. Git and database writes require recovery coordination; they are not assumed to share one transaction. Retrying a boundary reuses its identity and cannot double-count progress. Record a failure without creating a success event or moving head.

Save-point failure marks evidence stale and blocks admission until repaired. It does not undo already accepted source publication. Resume reconciles durable workflow and worktree state before scheduling new work.

rows: Fetch/import/index failure
Keep successful stage results and cursors; required stages block admission, optional gaps remain visible.
Source conflict or validation failure
Retain staging and diagnostic evidence; keep accepted head unchanged until reconciliation succeeds.
Crash during source application
Recover Git position and state publication as one coordinated operation; never assume Git and SQL share a transaction.
Repeated command or boundary retry
Use stable operation IDs; do not duplicate integration, timeline entries, imports, or counted gains.
Pause or restart
Reconcile leases, claims, accepted worktree, and pending publication; keep desired pause and history.
Canonical worktree and head
Harness source state.
Upstream lineage
Accepted upstream revision and timeline source transitions.
Historical measurements
Save points pinned to their source and build inputs.
Workflow and trace links
Stable run, epoch, Sync, event, and kernel trace identities.
Admission and pause
Desired execution state plus readiness and blockers.

text.insert: Preserve event, command, correlation, run, epoch, and trace identities when state is reorganized. Recorded evidence remains attached to its original source revision. The current harness timeline supplies durable ordering and links to retained Agent Kernel traces.
